senses: A loss with no points scored.
ety: Clipping of schneider, from German Schneider (“tailor”).

senses: A person who specializes in criminal law.
A person who specializes in the collection and examination of forensic evidence at a crime scene.
Suffering from or characterized by hyperinsulinemia, an excessively high level of insulin in the blood
Somewhat reddish or reddish-brown in colour (especially of hair or skin colouring).
Having reddish-brown hair. (of a person)
Having a flavour or aroma of the spice ginger; containing that spice.
Energetic, vigorous, lively, peppy, zippy.
Ginger, inhibited, cautious.
examples: He was a small, thick man, with a great rounded, bald head and one thin border of gingery curls.
The boys have made themselves very popular with the fans here, because a good, gingery gaffe is played all the time, regardless of the score.
The recent showing of the locals has been a big disappointment to the fans, the team playing loosely, and the gingery coaching and hustling of Hulswitt has been the only redeeming feature.

senses: A kind of smaller Russian button accordion.
ety: From Russian гармо́нь (garmónʹ), cognate to English harmonica.

senses: Any act of public molestation or offense, usually of a sexual nature, against unsuspecting victims.
A person, usually a man, who rubs against or gropes others, usually women, in crowds, often in trains, to attain sexual pleasure.
A geochemical of biological origin.
The wife of a sharif.
One who gnashes the teeth.
Long-lasting.
ety: From duration + -ive. Alternatively, borrowed from French duratif, from Old French duratif (“lasting continuously (for a certain time)”), via Anglo-Norman French, and existing in the form duratif from about the twelfth through the fourteenth centuries, when the spelling was altered to durative under the influence of the literary Neolatin movement. Analogous to dure (“to last, to continue”) + -ive.

senses: To bid (command or summon) again.
To bid again on something.
To require a new set of bids for.
To bid a higher value of the current suit.
examples: Alicia was surprised that Stefan had rebidden the Count from the shades.
We had to rebid the contract when accusations of fraud by other competitors occurred.

senses: An industrial solvent, often containing polyhalogenated hydrocarbons, used to remove grease from mechanical parts.
A machine that accomplishes this task.
A breed of beef cattle.
The shafts or thills of a wagon or carriage.
ety: For the obsolete limmer, from Old Norse limar (“branches”), plural of lim.

senses: To represent as a villain.
The art and technology of producing moving (video) images on photosensitive surfaces, and its digital counterpart.
The occupation of making videos.
The list of music videos an artist has appeared or performed in.
The bluish-green colour of the sea.
A transparent bluish-green, sometimes yellow-green, variety of beryl.
ety: From Latin aqua marīna (“sea water”), adjective form from mare (“sea”).

senses: A man who serves in the armed forces.
A person, especially a man, employed in service and maintenance of equipment.
A yeast dough bread pocket with a filling of beef, pork, cabbage or sauerkraut, onions, and seasonings.
ety: Trade name, said to have been introduced by Sally Everett (née Brening), who began selling them in Lincoln, Nebraska, in 1949. Possibly from Krautrunz, an older German name for the bierock, or Low German runsa, "belly", alluding to its rounded shape; compare modern German Ranzen (“belly”).

senses: Having two axes.
Along two axes; e.g. in engineering, a shear or compression text of a material along two axes

Having a value in two perpendicular directions. (In solid mechanics, it generally means that normal stresses exist in two of the possible three directions, though not necessarily equal in sign or magnitude.)
An entertainer skilled in the art of escapology.
A drug or substance that acts upon the nerves.
A miniature virginal, pitched one octave higher than the larger version.
The (often sexual) enjoyment of receiving pain or humiliation.
ety: From German Masochismus, coined alongside Sadismus in 1886 by Richard von Krafft-Ebing in his book Psychopathia Sexualis. Named after Leopold von Sacher-Masoch, whose novel "Venus in Furs" explores a sadomasochistic relationship, + -ism.

senses: The phenomenon, in chemistry, physics and mathematics, in which objects are mirror images of each other, but are otherwise identical; handedness.
A person who implements something.
A bar mounted on the roof of a vehicle, such as a police car, with rotating beacons or other lights to provide a visual warning.
Ovis ammon, the largest wild sheep, which roams the highlands of Central Asia.
Subsequent to the menopause.
Having experienced menopause.
A top-fermented barley/wheat beer brewed mainly in Belgium and the Netherlands.
Cracklings from rendered chicken fat.
ety: From the same root as greaves, graves (“residue left after rendering animal fat”) and gribenes (“chicken cracklings and onions”). Compare older dialectal northern (Low) German forms like greven and greeven.

senses: Control of both industry and government by labor unions, especially as achieved through revolutionary direct action; advocacy for attempts to bring it about.
A Puerto Rican frozen dessert, shaped like a pyramid, made of shaved ice and covered with fruit-flavored syrup.
ety: From Puerto Rican Spanish piragua, from pirámide (“pyramid”) + agua (“water”).

senses: Articles used in the preparation and drinking of tea.
Characteristic of or suitable to a creature, often specifically a non-human animal.
examples: Bracketed by two roiling group passages, smaller dances slink by, marked by much creaturely creeping and carnivorous eroticism.
Crammed like a biblical ark with creaturely wonders, “The Birds of America” conveys a sense of summation, although its chronicle of American bird life is far from complete.

senses: To find the latitude and longitude coordinates of an address.
examples: I geocode my customers' addresses to provide them with more relevant promotional material.

senses: Any strong, permeable fabric used in earthworks for any of a number of purposes, including separation of soil layers, filtering, reinforcing, erosion protection and protection of drainage pipes from clogging.
examples: You need to excavate and remove the topsoil, line the subsoil with a geotextile, then lay and compact hardcore.
The design also included geotextile lining of the trench in which the drainage pipe was buried.

senses: Any of several types of informal cooperative society.
Such a group for pooling and investing savings.
A nanoscale leaf (part of a larger structure) that converts wind and solar energy into electricity
Especially, Vitex rotundifolia, native to Pacific seashores in Asia and Oceania, widely introduced in similar environments.
ety: Borrowed from translingual Vitex, from Latin vītex.
